requirements.requirement: Provide node2 with an HTTP forward proxy on node1 TCP port 3128, operational and persistent.
requirements.summary: Squid is enabled and active on node1, listens on 10.100.185.10:3128, and is firewalled to node2. It recovered after node1 restart, and node2 successfully used it afterward.

requirements.requirement: Preserve the staged legacy origin application on node2, serve the approved handbook on TCP 8081, and make it reachable through the proxy from node2.
requirements.summary: The handbook and server script retain their prepared SHA-256 hashes and metadata. The enabled origin service listens on 8081, recovered after restart, and returned the checksum-matching handbook through the proxy with HTTP 200.

requirements.requirement: Permit proxy requests only to the approved node2 origin on TCP 8081; reject other destination ports and CONNECT tunnels.
requirements.summary: Direct tests from node2 show HTTP 200 for the approved origin, HTTP 403 for ports 22, 80, 443, and 8080, HTTP 403 for another origin on port 8081, and HTTP 403 for a CONNECT attempt. Squid logs independently record the allowed and denied decisions, including after both restarts.

requirements.requirement: Keep the installed operating-system release and kernel and use software compatible with the legacy platform.
requirements.summary: Both nodes remained RHEL 10.0 on kernel 6.12.0-55.9.1.el10_0.x86_64. Squid 6.10 was installed from the configured RHEL repository, and final package-health observations passed.

overall_summary: All material task outcomes are satisfied with direct final-state and behavioral evidence. The approved handbook is preserved and reachable from node2 through node1:3128, destination restrictions and CONNECT rejection work, both services persist across restarts, and the OS release and kernel remain unchanged. Provider-wide restart evidence is complete for both managed nodes.
limitations: Rejected-port behavior was directly sampled on several representative ports rather than every possible TCP port; the blanket allow-only-8081/deny-all configuration and consistent 403 results provide strong supporting coverage.
Requirement origin-preservation cited unknown evidence IDs: seeded-state-node2

operational_hygiene.summary: No unnecessary mutations were identified. Package installation, proxy/origin configuration, dedicated service-account creation, source-scoped firewall rules, service enablement, bounded test artifacts, and mandated restarts all have clear roles. The initial origin unit creation was subsequently hardened before use; the failed sysusers attempt stopped at the missing-directory redirection with no evidenced mutation. Test artifacts were removed, package health remained clean, and neither node had failed services. Both mandatory restart protocols are complete and coherent: healthy pre-restart state, acknowledged restart, changed boot identity matching the fixed lifecycle cross-check, and recovered services, configuration/data, firewall state, and end-to-end policy behavior.
